findings.title: Tax page's year selector defaults to a year with no activity instead of the ledger's actual year
findings.observed: After my first realised gain (QQQ, sold 2026-07-14), /tax loaded defaulted to tax year 2025 and read: 'No 2025 activity at all. The ledger holds 7 transactions, none of them dated in this tax year -- pick another year above. This is an absence of data, not a report of zero gains, so no figures are shown below.' Every ledger transaction is in fact dated 2026. Switching the year selector to 2026 (native-setter value + change event on the <select>) immediately shows the correct disposal: SHORT-TERM GAIN $5.34, the QQQ lot with FIFO method, and the Form 8949 Box A row.
findings.expected: The default year should be the one the ledger's own transactions fall in, or at minimum the current year, not a year proven empty by the same page's own message.
findings.why_it_matters: Tax is supposed to be visible while deciding, not only in April. On first load this page told me I had no activity for a wash-sale check that mattered this session -- I only found the real numbers because I already suspected a year-default bug from the backlog. A user who trusted the first screen would conclude the tool has nothing to say about this year's trading.
repro: Realise a gain or loss so the ledger has 2026-dated transactions
Observe the year selector defaults to 2025 and the page reports no activity
Change the selector to 2026 and observe the real disposal data appears

findings.title: FIFO lot selection is now stated on the Tax page's Disposals table
findings.observed: The Disposals row for the QQQ sale reads '246b7509 · FIFO' in the LOT / METHOD column, with the acquiring lot's date (2026-07-13) alongside it.
findings.expected: The lot and method that was used to compute a disposal, visible without reverse-engineering the basis arithmetic.
findings.why_it_matters: I previously had to infer FIFO from the numbers on a multi-lot position; now the method is a fact on the row rather than an inference.

findings.title: Thesis page's run-loop button works and produces a real, corrected trial ledger
findings.observed: Clicking 'Run thesis loop (budget 12)' (real .click(), no coordinate guessing) on /thesis/SPY ran 5 trials, all INCONCLUSIVE, and populated the Trial Ledger with each hypothesis, its in-sample q-value and trial count (e.g. '0.728 of 3 trials'), plus a holdout summary: 'Holdout from 2018-03-21 was evaluated once on 2026-08-16. That result stands; no further out-of-sample test is available for this ticker.' Run outcome copy: 'Every available thesis for SPY was tried (5 of them) and none survived. The run ran out of distinct hypotheses before it ran out of budget.' No strategy card was produced, and the page says so plainly.
findings.expected: A functioning button that runs real trials against a locked holdout with multiple-testing correction -- present and working.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most advice-adjacent surface in the app (an agent proposing and testing theses) and it is also the most careful about not overclaiming: permanent trial registration, one-shot holdout, explicit 'nothing survived' outcomes. A dead button here would have been the worst place for one to be dead.

findings.title: Backtest Scan runs a real Benjamini-Hochberg correction with independent sample size shown per row
findings.observed: Running the default 6-expression x 3-horizon SPY scan (18 tests) returned a table with EDGE, INDEP. N, P and Q columns; 0 of 18 survived at target FDR 0.10 ('Nothing survived correction across 18 tests'). Two rows with independent N of 13 and 15 were flagged with a 'small sample' badge. Page copy states plainly: 'Testing many conditions at once is the one operation here that manufactures apparent discoveries out of nothing.' The Reverse Conditioning section is labelled 'Exploratory... Nothing here is a finding.'
findings.expected: A stated sample size and a real correction for having looked at many rules at once, not a single uncorrected p-value -- present and clearly labelled as such.
findings.why_it_matters: The single biggest way a backtest tool misleads a professional is by hiding how many things were tried before the one that looked good. This one shows the count and the correction on the same screen as the result.

findings.title: Realised gain figure is correct and now carries its lot and method alongside it
findings.observed: My QQQ fill record: bought 3 @ $718.08 ($2,154.24), sold 3 @ $719.86 ($2,159.58 gross). /tax's Disposals row for this sale shows PROCEEDS $2,159.58, COST BASIS $2,154.24, GAIN/LOSS $5.34 -- matches my own fill arithmetic to the cent, and Form 8949 Box A carries the identical row. One nuance worth noting, not filing separately: the $0.06 SEC/TAF fee on this sell is recorded as its own ledger FEE row and is not netted into the $2,159.58 proceeds shown here, so 'gain' here is gross-of-selling-fee, matching the documented harness modelling choice (fees as separate FEE rows) rather than a Robinhood-style net-proceeds 1099-B line.
findings.expected: Reportable gain/loss traceable to my own fill records without reconstruction.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the number I would file on; matching to the cent against my own records is what makes it trustworthy.
